ANISOTROPY.rationale: Both structural rules and dimension chains are strongly axis-aligned and their anisotropy ranges overlap at every scale.

AXIAL_PERSISTENCE.rationale: Positive mean bilateral persistence is higher at local/meso scale, but every range overlaps and one hard negative is among the strongest wide-context runs.

CORRIDOR_OCCUPANCY.rationale: Binary axial occupancy is mildly higher for positives at meso/wide scale, but ranges overlap and raw-source occupancy reverses direction because surrounding page ink dominates.

LONG_RANGE_CONTEXT.rationale: Some positives persist farther on average, but wide-window persistence, support, anisotropy, and orientation all overlap materially with hard negatives.

OFF_AXIS_COMPLEXITY.rationale: Branches, junction proxies, components, off-axis ink, and tortuosity overlap; genuine nodes can be more complex than annotation glyphs.

TRANSVERSE_STABILITY.rationale: Width variation, cross-gap width change, drift, and shift overlap with inconsistent directions across masks and scales.

interpretation.geometry_authority: FinalStructure remains the single reconstruction authority
interpretation.next_evidence_candidate: Validated broader-context dimension-chain and text/glyph perception that recognizes annotation semantics (labels, repeated dimension layout, and associated markers), with calibrated uncertainty and advisory-only output.

small_interpretable_combination.reason: No feature supplies a stable class margin, and feature direction changes across source/binary representations or scale. A conjunction chosen to fit these eleven cases would be threshold overfitting rather than independent evidence.

method: Diagnostic-only measurements on the same D5/D6 qualified cases. Source Otsu ink and captured processing binary are measured independently at gap/stroke/processing-scale normalized local, meso, and wide windows. No score or production classifier is built.
